---
title: "Structures Data"
---

Research organizations — institutions, laboratories, teams — are a key part of the research information managed by CRISalid.
Getting them into the graph is often the first step, and it can involve some work: mapping your local identifiers, encoding the hierarchy, handling supervision relationships between units and institutions.
This page is here to help you through it.

## Two options to connect to institutional directories

[CRISalid directory bridge](https://github.com/CRISalid-esr/crisalid-directory-bridge) offers two ways to feed structure data into the knowledge graph.
Both produce the same AMQP message format consumed by the IKG middleware.

| Source | DAG | Best suited for |
|---|---|---|
| **LDAP directory** (SUPANN 2021) | `load_ldap_structures` | Institutions with a SUPANN-compliant directory |
| **Spreadsheet (CSV)** | `load_spreadsheet_structure` | Manual curation, institutions without LDAP, graduate schools, cross-institutional units |

---

## LDAP path

The `load_ldap_structures` DAG queries an LDAP directory filtered on SUPANN object classes and converts entries into IKG-compliant structure records.

Key LDAP attributes used: `supannCodeEntite` (identifier), `supannCodeEntiteParent` (hierarchy), `supannTypeEntite`, `supannRefId` (external identifiers such as ROR, NNS), `eduOrgLegalName`, `ou`, `description`, `businessCategory`, `labeledURI`.

Structures with `businessCategory=organization` are excluded — they do not map to any IKG structure type.

### CSV complement

When `OVERRIDE_LDAP_STRUCTURE_DATA_FROM_SPREADSHEET=True`, the DAG also reads a CSV file and merges it into the LDAP results: any non-empty CSV value overwrites the corresponding LDAP field, while LDAP values are kept where the CSV is blank.
Use it to supply fields that LDAP does not carry: national identifiers (NNS/RNSR, ROR, Wikidata), tutelle relationships, HAL collections, research classifications.
A CSV-only structure (absent from LDAP) is added to the result set; a structure with `generic_type=ignore` is dropped.

### Generating a CSV template from live LDAP

Rather than building the CSV from scratch, use the provided script to pre-fill it from your live directory:

```bash
APP_ENV=DEV python scripts/generate_structure_template.py --output data/structures.csv
```

The script connects to LDAP with the credentials defined in `.env.dev`, fetches all structures, and writes a CSV with one row per entry.
It maps the fields it can derive from LDAP (`local_id`, `short_labels`, `long_labels`, `descriptions`, `web`, `main_mission`, `inclusions`) and leaves the rest blank for you to fill in.
Redirect to stdout by omitting `--output`.

Once you have the template you can open it in a spreadsheet editor or edit it directly, then use the tools below to validate and sort it before ingestion.

---

## Spreadsheet path

The `load_spreadsheet_structure` DAG (in [crisalid-directory-bridge](https://github.com/CRISalid-esr/crisalid-directory-bridge)) reads a UTF-8 CSV file whose columns follow the CRISalid structures format.
This is the recommended path for structures that are not in the institutional LDAP, or for institutions that prefer to maintain a fully curated file.

### File format reference

The full column specification and annotation syntax (labels with language tags, relationship entries with supervision codes and date ranges) is documented on the wiki:

👉 [Import des données structures](https://www.esup-portail.org/wiki/spaces/ESUPCRISalid/pages/1673035787/Import+des+donn%C3%A9es+structures) on the CRISalid Esup Portail wiki

---

## Tooling for CSV files

Three standalone Python scripts are available in the repository to prepare and inspect a structures CSV — whether you use the LDAP+CSV combined path or the pure spreadsheet path.
They require only the standard library (no Airflow, no virtualenv).

### Fixing row ordering

The CSV is processed row by row, so any structure referenced in `inclusions` or `participations` must appear in an **earlier row** than the structure that references it.
If you have ordering violations — for example after inserting rows manually — the sort script rewrites the file in the correct topological order:

```bash
python .claude/commands/sort_structures.py path/to/structures.csv
```

The script uses Kahn's topological sort and preserves the original relative order of rows as much as possible.
If a circular dependency is detected it prints a warning and leaves the file unchanged.

### Validating the CSV

```bash
python .claude/commands/check_structures.py path/to/structures.csv
```

Prints all errors and warnings with row numbers, then exits with a non-zero status if errors are found.

What it checks:

- Required columns and fields
- `local_id` format (max 10 chars, alphanumeric / `-` / `_` / `:`)
- Duplicate `local_id` values; `generic_type=ignore` rows are only checked for duplicates
- National type compatibility with `generic_type` (fetched live from the IKG model)
- Mission fields (`main_mission` required and valid for units; warns if set on other types)
- Conditional identifier requirements (UAI for institutions; NNS or ROR for research units)
- Identifier format (bare ROR/ISNI IDs, RNSR pattern for NNS)
- Reference integrity — every `local-*` target must exist in the file
- Ordering — a referenced structure must appear in an earlier row
- Isolation — warns on teams and unit subdivisions with no parent
- Date annotation format (YYYYMMDD)
- Label language tags

### Visualising the hierarchy

```bash
python .claude/commands/visualize_structures.py path/to/structures.csv [output.html] \
  [--root-institution LOCAL_ID]
```

Generates a self-contained HTML file (no server required, opens in any browser).
`--root-institution` sets the root node used for the initial viewport centering and the default 1-level expanded view; omit it to start fully expanded.
If `output.html` is not specified, the file is written next to the CSV with the same basename.

#### What the visualiser shows

- The full structure hierarchy as a directed acyclic graph, laid out with a right-to-left dagre algorithm (root institution on the right, leaf teams on the left)
- Nodes colour-coded by `generic_type`: institution · institution subdivision · unit · unit subdivision · team
- Solid arrows for inclusion relationships (`part_of`); dashed arrows for participation/supervision relationships, colour-coded by role (main / associated / participating supervision)
- External institutions referenced as tutelles (identified by `uai-` prefixes in the participations column) are shown as a separate group at the top of the graph, with names looked up from the national ESR institutions reference file
- Structures marked `generic_type=ignore` are excluded from the graph

#### Interacting with the graph

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Double-click** a node | Expand or collapse its children |
| **Single-click** a node | Open the info panel: full name, type, mission, identifiers (NNS, ROR, UAI, ISNI, Wikidata, Scopus) |
| **Expand all / Collapse all** | Toolbar buttons |
| **Show/hide participation edges** | Toggle in the toolbar |
| **Show/hide external nodes** | Toggle in the toolbar |
| **Search** | Filter and highlight nodes by label or identifier |
| **Fit** | Reset the viewport to show all visible nodes |

#### As Claude Code slash commands

If you use [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) inside the `crisalid-directory-bridge` repository, the same tools are available as slash commands:

```bash
/check-structures path/to/structures.csv
/visualize-structures path/to/structures.csv [output.html]
```
